extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning algebraic geometry (schemes and sheaves)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, characterizations, and key properties of quasicoherent OX-modules on schemes (construction from distinguished affine bases, exactness properties, finiteness notions, tensor constructions, duals, supports, and related exercises). Targeted at readers proving or verifying statements about quasicoherent sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf on distinguished affine base determines unique sheaf (Theorem 13.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheaf on the distinguished affine base F^b determines a unique (up to unique isomorphism) sheaf F on X whose restriction to the affine base is F^b. Morphisms on the distinguished affine base determine morphisms of sheaves; OX-modules on the distinguished affine base yield OX-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via construction of stalks and the sheaf of compatible germs; only requires that the category of open sets with distinguished inclusions be filtered. For experts: this is an equivalence of categories between sheaves on the Zariski topology and sheaves on the distinguished affine base. Exercises: 13.3.A (sections determined by germs), 13.3.B and 13.3.C (functoriality and OX-module version).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections determined by germs on distinguished affine base (Exercise 13.3.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A section of a sheaf on the distinguished affine base is determined by its germs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the construction that shows F(U)=F^b(U) for U in the base and to prove uniqueness. (Think about restriction maps and identifications on stalks.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of quasicoherent sheaf via localization (13.3.3 and 13.3.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: An OX-module F is quasicoherent iff for every inclusion Spec A_f ⊂ Spec A (a distinguished open), the natural map α: Γ(Spec A, F) ⊗_A A_f → Γ(Spec A_f, F) is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently: a quasicoherent sheaf is the data of one module for each affine open such that modules on distinguished opens are obtained by localization. Exercise 13.3.D: show equivalence; this is the practical test for quasicoherence on affine covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections over principal open are localization (QCQS lemma style, Exercise 13.3.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is quasicompact and quasiseparated and F is quasicoherent, and f is a global function on X, then the restriction map Γ(X, F) → Γ(X_f, F) is precisely localization: Γ(X, F)_f ≅ Γ(X_f, F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof hint: use a finite affine cover and exactness of localization (apply an exact functor ⊗_{Γ(X,OX)} Γ(X,OX)_f to the exact Cech sequence). This is a key computational tool for global-to-local arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward of quasicoherent sheaves along qcqs morphisms is quasicoherent (Exercise 13.3.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is quasicompact and quasiseparated and F is quasicoherent on X, then π_*F is quasicoherent on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as an important corollary of 13.3.E; used repeatedly in practice. The qcqs hypothesis is essential in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf of nilpotents is quasicoherent (Exercise 13.3.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring A and element f, N(A_f) ≅ N(A)_f, so one can define a quasicoherent sheaf of nilpotents on any scheme X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives example of an ideal sheaf which is quasicoherent; used to show the nilpotent locus is finite type/coherent in Noetherian situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension-over-invertible-section property (Exercise 13.3.H)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is quasicompact quasiseparated, L is invertible with section s, and F is quasicoherent, then any section of F over X_s can be expressed as (global section)/s^n for n sufficiently large: sections over X_s extend to X after multiplying by a power of s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More precisely described using graded rings and modules: ⊕_{n≥0} Γ(X, L^{⊗ n} ⊗ F) and the localization at s; prove in affine case and then glue. Useful when working with complements of divisor-type opens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grothendieck topology (site) axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: A Grothendieck topology (site) is given by a category of 'open sets' and allowed inclusions, closed under fibered products, together with a specification of coverings satisfying: identity covers itself, pullbacks of covers are covers, and a cover of a cover is a cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivates working on distinguished affine base (which is a site but not a topology). One can define presheaves as contravariant functors on this category and sheaves via the usual glueing axioms interpreted with the chosen covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: QCoh_X is an abelian category (Section 13.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The quasicoherent sheaves on a scheme X form an abelian category QCoh_X: must check 0 ∈ QCoh_X, closure under finite sums, and closure under kernels and cokernels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to affine checks using the characterization of quasicoherent sheaves: on affines kernels and cokernels correspond to module kernels and cokernels, preserving localization and hence quasicoherence; exactness can be checked stalkwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check exactness on an affine cover (Exercise 13.4.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence of quasicoherent sheaves F → G → H on X is exact iff it is exact on every open set in any chosen affine cover of X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, taking sections over an affine open Spec A is an exact functor from QCoh_X (restricted to that open) to A-modules. Use this to test injectivity/surjectivity of maps of quasicoherent sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution: global sections left-exactness vs. affines
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking sections over an arbitrary open is only left-exact; exactness on the right (surjectivity) is guaranteed only when the open is affine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the reason cohomology (H^1 etc.) appears when taking global sections over non-affine opens. Expect H^1(Spec A, F) = 0 for affine Spec A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free subsheaf need not be subvector bundle (warning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Morphisms of vector bundles are more restrictive than morphisms of locally free sheaves: a locally free subsheaf of a locally free sheaf need not correspond to a subvector bundle (example on A^1_k with exact sequence 0 → t k[t] → k[t] → k → 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to avoid incorrect geometric intuitions: check cokernels/stalks to determine whether quotient is locally free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module-like constructions extend to QCoh (tensor, Sym, ∧, T•)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructions for modules (tensor product, tensor algebra T•, symmetric algebra Sym•, exterior algebra ∧•) extend to quasicoherent sheaves via their descriptions on affine opens: Γ(Spec A, ·) is the corresponding module construction; localization commutes appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., Γ(Spec A, F⊗G) ≅ M⊗_A N if M = Γ(Spec A, F) and N = Γ(Spec A, G); similarly for Sym and ∧ using universal properties. No sheafification required when working on the distinguished affine base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free in short exact sequences (Exercises 13.5.A and 13.5.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0 is a short exact sequence of quasicoherent sheaves and F' and F'' are locally free on an affine Spec A (free of ranks a and b), then F is locally free (rank a+b). Conversely, under finite rank hypotheses, various implications about which terms are locally free hold with specified matrix/block descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs reduce to linear algebra after choosing trivializing affine opens; transition functions can be interpreted as block upper triangular matrices. Use rank/determinant arguments to find opens where matrices simplify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product localization property (Exercise 13.5.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Spec A affine and modules M,N corresponding to quasicoherent sheaves F,G, Γ(Spec A, F⊗G) ≅ M⊗_A N, and for distinguished opens Spec A_f we have Γ(Spec A_f, F⊗G) ≅ M_f ⊗_{A_f} N_f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the algebraic underpinning for computing tensor products of quasicoherent sheaves locally; use universal algebra or explicit constructions to prove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant line bundle and behavior in exact sequences (Exercises 13.5.D–H)
rubrics_metrics.description: For locally free F of rank m, ∧^m F = det F is a line bundle; filtrations of Sym^r F and ∧^r F in short exact sequences lead to relations among determinants so that alternating products of determinants in a finite exact sequence are trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use block matrix interpretation locally and Exercise 13.5.F to relate ∧ and Sym constructions to short exact sequences; Exercise 13.5.H gives the alternating triviality formula for determinant bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasicoherent ideal sheaves correspond to closed subschemes (13.5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If i: X ↪ Y is a closed embedding, then the kernel I_{X/Y} = ker(O_Y → i_* O_X) is a quasicoherent sheaf of ideals; conversely, a quasicoherent ideal sheaf defines a closed subscheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare to Exercise 8.1.H and characterization of quasicoherent sheaves (13.3.D). This correspondence is central in constructing closed subschemes via ideal sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torsion-free and torsion quasicoherent sheaves (13.5.5–13.5.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module M is torsion-free if am=0 implies a is a zero-divisor or m=0; on a scheme, F is torsion-free if each stalk F_p is torsion-free. On reduced schemes, define torsion quasicoherent sheaves as those whose stalk at the generic point of every irreducible component is 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish the stalk-local (strict) torsion-free notion (Gr-EGA terminology) from other uses. Useful in curve theory and coherent-sheaf classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness notions: finite type, finitely presented, coherent (13.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A-module: (i) finitely generated, (ii) finitely presented (finite generators and relations), (iii) coherent (finitely generated and kernels of maps from finite free modules are finitely generated). On schemes: F is finite type/finitely presented/coherent if on every affine Spec A, Γ(Spec A, F) has the corresponding property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If A is Noetherian, the three notions coincide. Coherent sheaves form an abelian subcategory (Proposition 13.6.3). Check these properties on a single affine cover using localization/glueing (Exercises 13.6.C and 13.6.D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent modules form an abelian category (13.6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The coherent A-modules (and coherent sheaves on a scheme) are closed under finite sums, kernels, and cokernels, hence form an abelian subcategory of A-mod (or Mod OX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Noetherian case the proof is straightforward because submodules of finitely generated modules are finitely generated. For general A see §13.8 exercises referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of finite type quasicoherent sheaf is closed (Exercise 13.7.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a finite type quasicoherent sheaf on X, then Supp(F) is a closed subset of X. (In general a quasicoherent sheaf need not have closed support.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to affine case and choose finite generators of the module. Use this to deduce that for locally Noetherian X the nilpotent (fuzz) locus is closed and the reduced locus is open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom from a coherent source is quasicoherent (Exercise 13.7.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is coherent and G is quasicoherent, then Hom(F, G) is quasicoherent; if additionally G and OX are coherent, Hom(F,G) is coherent. Hom(F, –) is left-exact as a functor QCoh_X → QCoh_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On affines compute Hom_A(M,N) and check localization property Hom_A(M,N)_f ≅ Hom_{A_f}(M_f, N_f). An explicit counterexample shows failure without finite presentation hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duals and reflexivity of coherent sheaves (13.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For coherent F (and OX coherent), the dual F^∨ := Hom(F, OX) is coherent. The natural map F → (F^∨)^∨ need not be an isomorphism; when it is, F is called reflexive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes vector bundle duals; Exercise 13.7.C gives exact sequences of duals when one term is locally free. Beware examples where dual is zero (e.g., module supported at a point).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of Hom(–,E) when target locally free (Exercise 13.7.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 → F → G → H → 0 is exact with H locally free, then applying Hom(–,E) yields an exact sequence 0 → Hom(H,E) → Hom(G,E) → Hom(F,E) → 0 (i.e., exact on the right as well).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof is local: reduce to affines with H ≅ A^n so the short exact sequence splits and Hom preserves exactness. Use when dualizing exact sequences involving locally free sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric Nakayama: local generation from fiber (Exercise 13.7.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a scheme, F a finite type quasicoherent sheaf, p ∈ X, and a_1,...,a_n ∈ F(U) whose images generate the fiber F_p ⊗ κ(p), then there exists an affine neighborhood Spec A of p on which the a_i generate F(Spec A) and hence generate all stalks and fibers over that neighborhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: if the fiber at p is 0 then F vanishes on a neighborhood of p. This is the geometric form of Nakayama's Lemma; reduce to the affine case and use Nakayama.
